boundary.title: Execution Boundary
boundary.subtitle: First identify what is driving this agent and which device it is bound to, then separate current-space configuration from capabilities that only belong to the current Electron control device.
boundary.builtinDesc: This agent is driven by the TabTin built-in engine, but this page still needs to distinguish between current-space configuration and host capabilities provided by this Electron instance. Local runtime only equals the agent's direct runtime when this Electron device is the execution device.
boundary.externalDesc: This agent is driven by an external engine. It mainly relies on its own tool system and terminal access, so the TabTin runtime, MCP, and Core CLI shown here describe what the current Electron host can provide, not what the external agent can always call directly.
boundary.boundLocal: This Electron device is the execution device
boundary.boundOther: This Agent is bound to another device
boundary.unbound: This Agent is not bound to an execution device yet

scope.executionTruthDesc: The runtime and MCP sections below prefer the fine-grained snapshot reported by the bound execution device heartbeat, so they can reflect the real state on a remote daemon or the currently bound host.
scope.spaceMountedDesc: This includes enabled sub-agents, connected extensions, and the skills visible after current-space eligibility filtering.
scope.localDirectDesc: Because this Electron instance is the execution device, the runtime and MCP below use live local reads and can be treated as execution-device truth.
scope.localHostedDesc: Even though this Electron instance is the execution device, when the agent uses an external backend the local runtime and local MCP shown below should still be treated as host capabilities, not capabilities the external agent can always call directly.
scope.localInventoryDesc: The bound device has not reported a fine-grained runtime snapshot yet. Until that happens, the current Electron host only shows space configuration and local CLI, and no longer pretends its own runtime or MCP is the remote execution truth.

runtime.title: Execution Device Runtime
runtime.direct: Because this Electron instance is the execution device, this runtime tools list comes from live local reads and can be treated as the agent's execution environment.
runtime.reported: This runtime tools list comes from the latest heartbeat reported by the bound execution device, so it reflects the real execution surface on a remote daemon or the currently bound host.
runtime.unbound: This Agent is not bound to an execution device yet, so there is no execution runtime to inspect here.
runtime.unavailable: A fine-grained runtime snapshot is not available from the bound execution device yet. This page will no longer pretend local inventory is the remote execution truth.
runtime.snapshotMissing: Once the bound device upgrades to the new heartbeat snapshot flow, its real runtime tools will appear here.
runtime.snapshotUnbound: Bind an execution device first to see its runtime tools here.
runtime.empty: No runtime tools could be read.
runtime.emptyUnknown: The bound device has not reported a runtime snapshot yet.

coreCli.title: Local Core CLI
coreCli.subtitle: These commands run through the local terminal on the machine hosting the current Electron control app. They are useful for manual debugging and also work as a fallback entry for external agents.
coreCli.recommendedSubtitle: For integrations and manual debugging, start from Workspace discovery first, then drill down into a concrete table or SQL flow.

recommendedSteps.discoverSpaces: Start by listing the Workspaces visible to this account
recommendedSteps.discoverTables: Then discover tables inside the current Workspace
recommendedSteps.inspectTable: Only after that, drill down into a concrete query within the current Workspace

extensionCli.title: Extension CLI
extensionCli.subtitle: This shows CLI commands declared dynamically by extensions and marks whether the extension is currently connected to this space.

localMcp.title: Execution Device MCP
localMcp.subtitle: Because this Electron instance is the execution device, this section reads local MCP state from the current control host.

localMcp.unboundSubtitle: This Agent is not bound to an execution device yet, so there is no execution MCP state to inspect here.
localMcp.snapshotMissing: The bound device has not reported an MCP snapshot yet, so this page no longer pretends the current Electron host MCP is the remote execution state.
localMcp.empty: Execution-device MCP is running but no tools are currently exposed.
localMcp.emptyUnknown: The bound device has not reported an MCP snapshot yet.

mounted.title: Mounted Capabilities
mounted.subtitle: This shows capability layers actually configured for the current space, plus the skills visible under current-space eligibility rules. It is a different layer from the local host capabilities shown above.
mounted.skillsHint: These are the skills visible after current-space eligibility filtering. They do not mean every listed skill is already fully enabled.
mounted.extensionHint: There are Extension CLI declarations, but this space has not enabled the matching extension connections yet.
mounted.localMcpHint: This shows the local MCP connections that are both mounted to the current space and enabled; the built-in agent uses them through mcp_call_tool.

auto_condense.label: Full-context summary
auto_condense.desc: The current Agent writes a summary with full access to all original messages and tool call details — best information retention, but costs one extra conversation turn

native.label: Quick summary
native.desc: A separate AI call summarizes old messages without using a turn. Faster, but each message is truncated to plain text (max 6000 chars) and structured data like tool calls is lost

prune_only.label: Direct discard
prune_only.desc: Removes the oldest messages to free space without calling AI. Fastest and cheapest, but deleted content cannot be recovered

advanced.compressionTriggerHint: Start compression when conversation fills this percentage of context window
